subject: `edit.toggle_step_input` on a Japanese Logic, and the two label gaps that kept it from State A
question: The operation was proved working live at three heads. Does it work on a Logic that is not English?

host.note: AppleLanguages set to `ja` and Logic relaunched; the project was reopened from File > 最近使った項目を開く. Restored afterwards.

reverify.command: python3 Scripts/livekit/live_778_step_input_toggle_reaches_its_menu_item.py <worktree> <head> (with LPM_EVIDENCE_ROOT exported, and `defaults write com.apple.logic10 AppleLanguages -array ja` plus a Logic relaunch beforehand)
reverify.expected: State A with `observed_open` flipping true then false, and Logic's window list carrying `ステップインプットキーボード` between the two calls
reverify.cost: about three minutes, plus a Logic relaunch either side of the language change

method: The harness was run unchanged against a Japanese Logic at three successive heads. The first run used the binary that had passed three English runs; the second added the Japanese menu-bar titles; the third added the window title. Each run's `observed` field was read rather than its pass/fail, because the operation's STATE is what distinguishes the two causes — a failure to find the menu and a failure to read back look the same from the check.

observations.what: what the operation answered on a Japanese Logic, by head

rows.detail: element_not_found · 'Window > Step Input Keyboard was not found.'

rows.windows_between_calls: lpm-locale-campaign - ステップインプットキーボード, lpm-locale-campaign - トラック

observations.what: the two labels, and where each was measured

rows.label: stepInputKeyboardWindowTitle
rows.added: ステップインプットキーボード
rows.source: live window list during this run — no census can hold it

conclusion: The operation was dead in Japanese for two independent reasons, and fixing the first exposed the second. `windowMenuBar` had no Japanese name, so the drive could not open the menu the item lives in — and the refusal named the English path, which reads as a missing item rather than a missing menu. With that fixed the AX channel found the item, pressed it and the window opened; then `stepInputKeyboardWindowTitle` could not see it, the channel polled twenty times, gave up with State C, and the chain fell through to the key-command destination, which toggles the window but reads nothing back. So the operation reported State B `readback_unavailable` about a window that was plainly open. The second gap is the interesting one: it is a WINDOW title, and the window does not exist until the operation opens it, so no navigation-free census can ever carry it. Three censuses and two rounds of menu-label work could not have found it; only driving the operation in that locale could.
limits: One language. Korean has all three labels and was not re-driven here, so this says nothing about whether the same chain reaches State A there.

The record of 2026-09-05 said the dead toggle was 'not a locale failure'. That was true of the cause it measured and wrong as a statement about the operation: two of the three gaps were locale gaps. It is superseded rather than corrected in place.

WHY the key-command destination cannot read back is still not established — whether that is by design for that channel or a missing readback. The fall-through itself is now observed, which the earlier record could not see.
State A on a Japanese Logic is not yet demonstrated in this record; the run that should show it comes after this change.
